name: fastmail-mcp
description: Unofficial MCP server for Fastmail API integration (not affiliated with or endorsed by Fastmail)

fastmail_api_token.title: Fastmail API Token
fastmail_api_token.description: Fastmail API token (Settings → Privacy & Security → API tokens)

fastmail_base_url.title: Fastmail Base URL
fastmail_base_url.description: Fastmail API base URL (leave default unless using a custom endpoint)

fastmail_download_dir.title: Attachment Download Directory
fastmail_download_dir.description: Incoming direction: the directory download_attachment WRITES saved attachments into (defaults to ~/Downloads/fastmail-mcp/). Every write is confined to this directory and cannot escape it. This setting has no effect on sending — files attached to outgoing mail are read from the separate Attachment Send Directory.

fastmail_attach_dir.title: Attachment Send Directory
fastmail_attach_dir.description: Outgoing direction: the directory files attached to outgoing mail are READ from, the mirror image of the Attachment Download Directory. Leave it unset and the send-an-attachment capability is disabled entirely — there is no default and no directory is created for you; the compose tools reject an attachment path until this is set. When set, it is a confinement boundary rather than a convenience default: a bare filename or relative path resolves inside it, and an absolute path outside it is rejected. Keep it separate from the download directory unless you deliberately want a downloaded file to be emailable straight back out; the two are resolved independently on purpose.

fastmail_allow_blob_attach.title: Allow Attaching Content Already In The Account
fastmail_allow_blob_attach.description: Outgoing direction, separate from the Attachment Send Directory: allow outgoing mail to attach content the account already holds — a blob id, or one part of an existing message — instead of only files read off local disk. Nothing is read from disk on those sources, so the send directory has no say over them and this is their own opt-in. Off by default; turning it on takes effect after a restart.

fastmail_timezone.title: Timezone
fastmail_timezone.description: Full IANA timezone name (e.g. America/New_York) - must contain a region-qualifying slash, or be exactly UTC; an abbreviation such as EST or NZ is rejected and stops the server from starting rather than being guessed at. Renders email date fields in local time with a UTC offset, reads date-only list_calendar_events windows as local days, and is the zone create_calendar_event writes a designator-less start/end in. Defaults to the server host's timezone.

fastmail_caldav_username.title: CalDAV Username
fastmail_caldav_username.description: Your Fastmail account email address, used for CalDAV calendar access. Optional, but every calendar tool needs it together with the CalDAV app password: with either one missing the calendar tools are unavailable and report how to configure them. Mail, contact and attachment tools are unaffected.

fastmail_caldav_password.title: CalDAV App Password
fastmail_caldav_password.description: App-specific password for CalDAV (Settings → Privacy & Security → Manage app passwords), used with the CalDAV username. Not your account login password, and not the JMAP API token. Optional: without it the calendar tools are unavailable.

fastmail_caldav_display_name.title: Calendar Organizer Display Name
fastmail_caldav_display_name.description: Display name shown as the ORGANIZER on calendar events you create with participants. Defaults to the CalDAV username when unset.
